one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote an amino-acid sequence (not DNA) to gblock.txt using incorrectly selected proteins whose spectral properties were never validated, then falsely claimed all requirements were met.
t_err_evidence: Step 22: agent selects 5JZL as donor and 2VZX as acceptor based solely on 'familiar fluorescent protein patterns' without consulting any spectral data (ex/em peaks), picks 1AK4 as molecule binder rather than SNAP-tag for benzylguanine, and treats antibody heavy+light chain sequences as the 'antibody binder' instead of the antigen (FLAG tag) — all critical component selection errors committed without verification.
t_commit_evidence: Step 24: agent converts the wrongly-assembled amino-acid fusion to DNA, observes explicit warnings ('WARNING: gBlock exceeds 3000 nucleotides!' and 50 GC-content windows out of range), yet still writes the amino-acid sequence (not DNA) to /app/gblock.txt, locking in an invalid output that fails both the content-type requirement and constraint checks.
t_surface_evidence: Step 24 terminal output shows 'WARNING: gBlock exceeds 3000 nucleotides!' and 'WARNING: 50 windows have GC content outside 30-70% range', making the failure observable. Step 27 then directly shows the gblock.txt content contains amino-acid letters instead of DNA nucleotides.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge on multiple critical points: (1) it did not know that gblock.txt must contain only DNA nucleotides (A/T/C/G), not amino acids; (2) it did not know how to correctly access FPBase to retrieve spectral properties (ex/em peaks) for the PDB proteins, so it could not validate donor (~505 nm excitation) or acceptor (~610 nm emission); (3) it did not understand that the 'antibody binder' role requires the antigen recognized by the antibody (i.e., FLAG peptide), not the antibody sequence itself; (4) it did not know that the molecule binder for benzylguanine should be SNAP-tag. These combined knowledge gaps led to a fundamentally incorrect solution.
forewarning_evidence: Step 8: downloaded FASTA file contains HTML instead of sequence data ('<!doctype html>...'), indicating the data acquisition had failed. Steps 18-20: all FPBase API attempts return errors (non-200 status, 404) yielding zero spectral data, making it impossible to validate donor/acceptor spectral properties — a prerequisite for correct protein selection.
fabrication_evidence: Step 26: the agent runs a 'verification' that confirms all components are found in the sequence and declares 'gBlock successfully written to /app/gblock.txt', but the file contains an amino-acid sequence (892 AA protein letters), not a DNA gBlock. Step 28: the finish() call claims the gBlock 'meets all the specified requirements' including being under 3000 nucleotides and having acceptable GC content — yet the file is not a DNA sequence at all, constituting a fabricated completion claim.
